newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Citibank's A$ debt issue offers good value -ANZ.
newsitem.headline: Citibank's A$ debt issue offers good value -ANZ.

text.p: Citibank Ltd's A$150 million five-year debt issue announced on Wednesday offers good value to investors if price talk of 36 to 38 basis points over government bonds is correct, ANZ Investment Bank said on Thursday.
The transferable certificates of deposit (TCD) drawn down from Citibank Ltd's, the Australian subsidiary of U.S. based Citicorp N.A., A$500 million funding programe are due to be priced on Monday.
"The recently announced Citibank issue compares favourably with other issues of similar maturity," ANZ Investment Bank in a research document.
"With a fair value of 35-36 basis points over bond, the price talk of 36-38 is very reasonable."
The TCDs mature March 15, 2002 and carry a 7.0 percent coupon, and the programme was rated AA minus by Standard & Poor's on Wednesday.

ANZ Investment Bank said recent comparable issues are the A-plus rated November 2001 by BOS International, and the AA-minus rated March 2002 by Merrill Lynch, both at a trading margin of 38 basis points over bond.

"The BOS issue should trade slightly outside Merrill Lynch and Citibank because of the rating difference. The maturity is negligible. Additionally, Citibank, a licensed bank in Australia, should be flat to or inside Merrill Lynch," ANZ Investment Bank said.
